simple.meaning: הוֹלֵלָה (hôwlêlâh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “folly.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 4 times across Ecclesiastes, beginning at Ecclesiastes 1:17. Its contexts include family line, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to הוֹלֵלָה (H1947).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: הוֹלֵלָה (hôwlêlâh) / H1947 is traced through Ecclesiastes 1:17, Ecclesiastes 2:12, Ecclesiastes 7:25, Ecclesiastes 9:3 as a generated source-based concept entry.

firstOccurrence.englishText: I applied my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly. I perceived that this also was a chasing after wind.

majorEvents.label: Genealogy
majorEvents.evidenceText: This is an evil in all that is done under the sun, that there is one event to all: yes also, the heart of the sons of men is full of evil, and madness is in their heart while they live, and after that they go to the dead.

timeline.evidenceText: I applied my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly. I perceived that this also was a chasing after wind.
I turned myself to consider wisdom, madness, and folly; for what can the king’s successor do? Just that which has been done long ago.
I turned around, and my heart sought to know and to search out, and to seek wisdom and the scheme of things, and to know that wickedness is stupidity, and that foolishness is madness.

This is an evil in all that is done under the sun, that there is one event to all: yes also, the heart of the sons of men is full of evil, and madness is in their heart while they live, and after that they go to the dead.

definitions.full: H1947. holelah [ הוֺלֵלָה ] noun feminine madness (on text see below), only plural הוֺלֵלוֺת הֹלֵלוֺת, , and only Ecclesiastes: Eccl 1:17 and I set my heart ( לִבִּי וָאֶתְּנָה ) to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly ( וְשִׂכְלוּת הֹלֵלוֺת ), compare הוֺלֵלוֺת 2:12 (|| id. ); ה וְהַסִּכְלוּת כֶּסֶל רֶשַׁע ׳וְלָדַעַת 7:25 ; i.e. to know folly to be madness; possibly read חוֺלֵלוּת , compare סִכְלוּת & following; the moral evil of it is specifically recognized in 9:3 (|| רָע ).
